queries.search_text: site:single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu European Payment Observatory annual report 2025 late payments businesses
queries.proposition: The European Commission reports that more than half of EU companies had difficulties from late payments in 2024, supplier-reported B2B and G2B payment periods exceeded 60 days, governments paid later than businesses, and collection created administrative burden; this supports testing workflows that make acceptance, disputes, and follow-up cheaper, but not any niche's willingness to pay.
queries.status: Official current evidence supports a broad and worsening loss event; product-level demand and Polish niche economics remain unproven.
queries.contradiction: Payment performance varies widely by Member State, the source does not validate any proposed vertical, and transparency or workflow software alone may not overcome buyer power or deliberate delay.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Recruit ten Polish SMEs across the five proposed niches through accountants and trade groups, process one real overdue or pre-invoice case each manually, and ask for a paid continuation only after a documented acceptance or resolution event.

queries.search_text: site:ure.gov.pl 2025 Poland dynamic electricity prices demand response flexibility energy storage prosumers
queries.source_title: Już ponad 4,8 tys. gospodarstw domowych korzysta z umów z cenami dynamicznymi
queries.proposition: Poland's energy regulator reports that in 2025 dynamic distribution tariffs linked price zones to system imbalance, 48% of customers had required remote-read meters, household dynamic contracts rose to 4,836, and small or microbusiness contracts reached 27,000; load profile materially affected realized prices, creating a testable coordination and qualification problem.
queries.status: Official market evidence supports growing technical availability and heterogeneous outcomes; it does not show demand for optimization products or guaranteed savings.
queries.contradiction: Household penetration remained below 0.03%, 2025 household users gave up a protected price, and annual average prices varied from 476 to 769 PLN/MWh across sellers, so generic savings claims would be unsafe and tariff protection may suppress adoption.
queries.cheapest_resolving_test: Obtain consented interval-meter data and bills from twenty households or microbusinesses, backtest actual available tariffs without controlling equipment, then seek three paid shadow-mode pilots from sites with demonstrably shiftable load.

concepts.title: Milestone Acceptance Rail for Public-Works Subcontractors
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A lightweight workflow assembles milestone evidence, identifies the person authorized to accept it, and issues the invoice immediately after recorded acceptance, charging the subcontractor per accepted packet without financing the receivable.
concepts.customer: Polish electrical, renewable, and construction subcontractors serving main contractors or public projects
concepts.loss_event: Completed work sits unbilled or disputed because acceptance evidence is incomplete or trapped with an unclear approver, extending the subcontractor's cash gap.
concepts.beneficiary: The subcontractor's owner and finance team
concepts.authority_holder: The contractually designated site inspector, main contractor, or contracting authority that can accept the milestone
concepts.distributor: Construction accountants, cost estimators, and renewable-installation partners
concepts.risk_bearer: The subcontractor retains payment and counterparty risk; the product gives no collection guarantee.
concepts.transaction_owner: The platform owns the evidence-to-acceptance workflow and fee event, while the contracting parties retain the underlying works and payment transaction.
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed fee when the first milestone packet is submitted through the workflow and formally accepted by the named authority holder
concepts.acquisition_route: Pilot with the founder's family renewable-installation firm, then sell through accountants serving regional subcontractors.
concepts.compounding_asset: A permissioned library of acceptance requirements, rejection reasons, and resolution paths by buyer and contract template
hypotheses: A meaningful share of delay begins before invoice due dates, at milestone acceptance.
Subcontractors will pay for faster acceptance without asking the vendor to fund receivables.
Contract-specific checklists can be produced from customer-provided documents with limited legal review.

constraint_class.constraint: Invoice, public-procurement, and contractual acceptance requirements
Access to buyer portals and signed site records
Supplier fear of irritating a powerful buyer

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No fabricated acceptance, backdating, impersonation of an approver, or promise that a compliant packet guarantees payment.

concepts.title: Reimbursement Hold Resolver for Small Clinics
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A privacy-preserving exception desk turns rejected or suspended public-payer claim batches into a prioritized document queue and charges a clinic only when the payer acknowledges a corrected batch.
concepts.customer: Independent Polish outpatient clinics and diagnostic practices billing a public payer
concepts.loss_event: A reimbursement batch is held because codes, referrals, signatures, or supporting documents do not match, while clinicians and billing staff lack time to identify the controlling exception.
concepts.beneficiary: The clinic and its patients through steadier operating cash flow
concepts.authority_holder: The public payer's claims rules and the clinic employee authorized to correct and resubmit records
concepts.distributor: Medical billing bureaux, practice-software vendors, and medical-accounting firms
concepts.risk_bearer: The clinic retains reimbursement risk and clinical responsibility.
concepts.transaction_owner: The service owns the exception-resolution case and outcome fee; the clinic owns and submits the claim.
concepts.first_paid_event: A case fee when the first corrected batch receives formal payer acknowledgment rather than merely when advice is delivered
concepts.acquisition_route: Use the medical-student partner to map nonclinical workflow and recruit billing managers through practice-software and accounting channels.
concepts.compounding_asset: A de-identified map from rejection codes and document states to successful correction sequences
hypotheses: Small clinics experience frequent document-driven holds large enough to buy outside help.
Payer acknowledgments can be observed reliably without storing unnecessary health data.
A nonclinical workflow can resolve enough cases without practicing medicine or law.

constraint_class.constraint: Health-data processing, medical records, and reimbursement rules
Access to payer interfaces and structured rejection data
Clinic willingness to share even minimized case information

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No upcoding, invented documentation, medical judgment, unauthorized patient-data use, or representation that the service can override payer decisions.

concepts.title: Freight Waiting-Time Proof to Invoice
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A mobile-light evidence workflow converts driver timestamps and dispatch records into contract-specific waiting-time charges, with the carrier paying a success fee only after the charge is accepted.
concepts.customer: Small road carriers and owner-operators serving larger forwarders or shippers
concepts.loss_event: Unplanned loading or unloading waits consume driver and vehicle capacity, but weak evidence or ambiguous authorization leaves the accessorial charge unbilled or disputed.
concepts.beneficiary: The carrier and driver whose lost capacity becomes billable
concepts.authority_holder: The shipper or forwarder contact authorized under the transport order to approve accessorial charges
concepts.distributor: Transport accountants, telematics resellers, and freight associations
concepts.risk_bearer: The carrier retains customer-relationship and payment risk.
concepts.transaction_owner: The platform owns evidence assembly, approval routing, and its success-fee invoice; it does not own the freight contract.
concepts.first_paid_event: A percentage or fixed fee after the first waiting-time charge receives written customer acceptance
concepts.acquisition_route: Offer accountants a manual recovery audit on recent completed loads, then convert repeat users to the workflow.
concepts.compounding_asset: A contract- and counterparty-specific map of admissible evidence, approval latency, and dispute outcomes
concepts.mechanism_class: Loss-bearer evidence capture tied to buyer acceptance
hypotheses: Carriers forgo collectible accessorial charges because proof is fragmented rather than because contracts categorically exclude them.
A written acceptance event is observable enough to support outcome-based billing.
Accountants and telematics vendors can distribute the service without high-touch networking.

constraint_class.constraint: Transport contract terms and debt-collection rules
Reliable timestamps and integration with dispatch or telematics systems
Fear of losing loads by asserting small charges

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No falsified geolocation, driver coercion, hidden surveillance, or collection activity requiring authorization the operator lacks.

concepts.title: Export Order Payment-Term Gate
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A pre-order policy engine uses a supplier's own payment history and contract facts to route each export order to prepayment, deposit, insurance review, or ordinary terms before production starts.
concepts.customer: Polish SME manufacturers and wholesalers selling repeatedly to foreign business buyers
concepts.loss_event: The supplier commits inventory and production before anyone owns the decision on buyer-specific payment terms, then carries a late or disputed cross-border receivable.
concepts.beneficiary: The supplier's owner, finance lead, and operations team
concepts.authority_holder: The supplier executive who approves commercial terms; insurers and buyers control their own approvals
concepts.distributor: Export accountants, customs agents, and freight forwarders
concepts.risk_bearer: The supplier retains buyer default and commercial risk unless it separately contracts with a licensed insurer or financier.
concepts.transaction_owner: The platform owns the internal approval record and charges per screened order; the supplier owns the sale and payment terms.
concepts.first_paid_event: A fee when the first live export order receives a documented payment-term decision before production release
concepts.acquisition_route: Distribute a spreadsheet-based payment-delay audit through export accountants and forwarders, then upsell recurring order gates.
concepts.compounding_asset: A permissioned outcome dataset connecting order attributes, chosen protections, payment timing, and dispute causes
concepts.mechanism_class: Risk-bearer decision rights moved before commitment
hypotheses: Many small exporters lack a consistently enforced payment-term authority gate.
Their own ledger and order data are predictive enough to improve decisions without creating a public credit score.
A per-order fee is cheaper than recurring late-payment administration.

constraint_class.constraint: Credit-information, insurance intermediation, sanctions, and cross-border contract requirements
Sparse internal histories for new buyers
Buyers may reject deposits or shorter terms

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No unlicensed lending or insurance advice, covert personal profiling, sanctions evasion, or unsupported claim that a routing decision predicts default.

concepts.title: Invoice Approval-Graph Desk for Service Firms
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A managed software desk maps who requested, received, approved, and can unblock each deliverable, then charges when an overdue invoice moves into an acknowledged resolution path.
concepts.customer: Small software agencies, consultancies, laboratories, and engineering service firms selling to larger organizations
concepts.loss_event: A completed deliverable and invoice bounce between procurement, project owner, and accounts payable because no one owns the exception, consuming founder time and delaying cash.
concepts.beneficiary: The firm's founder and finance team
concepts.authority_holder: The buyer's project owner, procurement approver, or accounts-payable exception owner identified by the contract
concepts.distributor: Bookkeepers, fractional CFOs, and vertical project-management consultants
concepts.risk_bearer: The service firm retains dispute, collection, and relationship risk.
concepts.transaction_owner: The desk owns the permissioned resolution case, communications log, and its fee trigger; neither debt nor buyer funds pass through it.
concepts.first_paid_event: A fixed fee when the first stalled invoice receives buyer acknowledgment plus a named next action and owner
concepts.acquisition_route: Give bookkeeping firms a co-branded aging-ledger triage that flags cases suitable for a paid resolution desk.
concepts.compounding_asset: An approval-graph corpus of role patterns, message sequences, and time-to-resolution by buyer type
hypotheses: A material subset of overdue invoices is stalled by routing failures rather than insolvency or substantive disputes.
Buyer acknowledgment and named ownership are valuable, auditable intermediate outcomes.
Bookkeepers can supply repeatable low-cost distribution.

constraint_class.constraint: Commercial communications, debt-collection boundaries, and data protection
Access to email, contracts, and accounts-receivable records
Escalation may strain a strategic account

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No harassment, false legal threats, impersonation, unauthorized mailbox access, or claim that acknowledgment means the debt is undisputed.

concepts.title: Cold-Store Dynamic Tariff Shadow Scheduler
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A read-only scheduler finds safe refrigeration and defrost windows against actual dynamic energy and network prices, charging a site for a validated shadow schedule before any automated control.
concepts.customer: Independent cold stores, grocers, bakeries, and food processors with shiftable refrigeration loads
concepts.loss_event: Rigid compressor and defrost schedules concentrate consumption in expensive intervals even when thermal inertia could shift load without harming product.
concepts.beneficiary: The site owner, with secondary system-flexibility benefits
concepts.authority_holder: The site's food-safety and operations manager sets temperature limits; the seller and DSO set applicable prices.
concepts.distributor: Refrigeration maintenance contractors and commercial energy brokers
concepts.risk_bearer: The site retains tariff and product-temperature risk during shadow mode and any later approved control.
concepts.transaction_owner: The platform owns schedule calculation, validation reporting, and subscription billing; it neither sells electricity nor dispatches assets initially.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid thirty-day shadow report after interval-meter and temperature data pass validation and a feasible savings schedule is delivered
concepts.acquisition_route: Equip refrigeration contractors with a pre-sales meter-data check and share revenue on converted shadow pilots.
concepts.compounding_asset: A site-type dataset linking interval load, temperature constraints, tariff intervals, and realized flexibility
concepts.mechanism_class: Beneficiary-controlled load shifting under explicit safety bounds
hypotheses: Enough microbusiness sites have remote-read meters and accessible interval data.
Refrigeration loads contain repeatable flexibility after mandatory temperature constraints.
Verified shadow savings are sufficient to convert sites to recurring service.

constraint_class.constraint: Food-safety temperature limits and equipment electrical requirements
Meter, sensor, and controller data access
Savings depend on tariff spread and actual flexible load

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No control outside approved temperature envelopes, safety bypass, fabricated baseline, or guaranteed savings claim.

concepts.title: Battery Commissioning Certificate for Solar Installers
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A vendor-neutral audit checks whether a home or small-business battery is configured for the customer's actual tariff, load, and warranty limits, with the installer paying per commissioning certificate.
concepts.customer: Polish photovoltaic and battery installers that want fewer callbacks and demonstrable commissioning quality
concepts.loss_event: A technically functional battery disappoints because default schedules ignore hourly prices, household load shape, backup needs, or warranty constraints, leaving the installer to absorb support and reputational costs.
concepts.beneficiary: The installer and the system owner
concepts.authority_holder: The system owner authorizes settings; the installer and equipment warranty define permissible configuration.
concepts.distributor: Battery and inverter wholesalers, installation networks, and renewable-industry accountants
concepts.risk_bearer: The equipment owner bears market-price risk, while the installer retains installation and warranty obligations.
concepts.transaction_owner: The service owns the audit and certificate transaction; the installer retains commissioning and any physical changes.
concepts.first_paid_event: An installer fee when the first system receives a signed, data-backed commissioning certificate with disclosed limits
concepts.acquisition_route: Validate on the family installation firm's jobs, then distribute the certificate through equipment wholesalers as an installer quality tool.
concepts.compounding_asset: A compatibility and outcome library across inverter models, tariff structures, load profiles, settings, and callback causes
hypotheses: Installers experience enough tariff-related callbacks to pay for independent commissioning evidence.
Common inverter exports expose sufficient data without unsupported control integrations.
Homeowners value a transparent certificate enough to improve installer conversion or referrals.

constraint_class.constraint: Electrical safety, consumer rights, and manufacturer warranty terms
Fragmented inverter APIs and firmware behavior
Installers may view external auditing as criticism

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No warranty override, unsafe battery cycling, unauthorized remote control, concealed tariff downside, or claim that certification guarantees bill savings.

concepts.title: Route-Safe Charging Windows for Small EV Fleets
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A depot scheduler translates next-day routes, charger limits, and dynamic tariffs into charge-by deadlines, with fleets paying per connected vehicle after a shadow plan proves route feasibility.
concepts.customer: Local delivery, service, and municipal-contractor fleets operating electric vans from a depot
concepts.loss_event: Vehicles charge as soon as they plug in, raising energy cost or coincident load, while generic optimization risks a missed morning route.
concepts.beneficiary: The fleet operator and dispatch team
concepts.authority_holder: The fleet dispatcher defines required state of charge and departure; the charger owner authorizes any control.
concepts.distributor: Commercial charger installers, vehicle-leasing firms, and fleet telematics providers
concepts.risk_bearer: The fleet retains route-service and tariff risk; the system defaults to meeting the declared departure constraint.
concepts.transaction_owner: The platform owns schedule generation, charger-command logging where authorized, and per-vehicle billing; it does not buy or resell electricity.
concepts.first_paid_event: A paid depot shadow pilot after the first week of schedules meets every declared route constraint in simulation
concepts.acquisition_route: Let charger installers bundle the pilot into post-installation handover and earn a recurring referral share.
concepts.compounding_asset: A depot-level dataset connecting route demand, weather, vehicle consumption, charger availability, and price-responsive flexibility
concepts.mechanism_class: Operational constraint translated into price-responsive dispatch
hypotheses: Small fleets have predictable overnight dwell but lack tariff-aware dispatch tooling.
Charger or telematics interfaces are accessible for a useful share of target fleets.
Avoided cost exceeds integration and support expense without compromising route readiness.

constraint_class.constraint: Charger electrical safety, employee access, and vehicle warranty terms
Charger, vehicle, and telematics interoperability
Tariff savings must exceed integration cost at small fleet scale

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No disabling safety controls, falsifying route readiness, accessing driver data beyond explicit purpose, or promising savings independent of actual tariffs and routes.

concepts.title: Verified Dynamic-Tariff Lead Exchange
concepts.one_sentence_thesis: A neutral calculator verifies meter eligibility and shiftable load before a consumer requests an offer, then charges an electricity seller only when a suitable customer activates a dynamic contract after required disclosures.
concepts.customer: Alternative electricity sellers seeking suitable household and microbusiness dynamic-tariff customers
concepts.loss_event: Sellers spend acquisition budget on customers lacking a remote-read meter, shiftable consumption, or informed risk tolerance, while unsuitable customers face bill shock and churn.
concepts.beneficiary: The seller and customers whose load profile genuinely fits the offer
concepts.authority_holder: The customer chooses the contract, the seller verifies and contracts, and the DSO controls meter eligibility data.
concepts.distributor: PV, battery, heat-pump, and EV-charger installers plus small-business accountants
concepts.risk_bearer: The seller bears the paid-lead risk; the customer retains price variability after transparent consent.
concepts.transaction_owner: The exchange owns consented qualification, attribution, and the activation-fee transaction; the licensed seller owns the energy contract.
concepts.first_paid_event: The seller pays for the first attributed contract that remains active after applicable withdrawal or cooling-off rights
concepts.acquisition_route: Embed the calculator in installer post-sale portals and accountant newsletters, avoiding camera-led consumer acquisition.
concepts.compounding_asset: A consented dataset of meter eligibility, load-shift features, offer selection, activation, churn, and realized bill outcomes
hypotheses: Alternative sellers will pay more for verified activations than for unqualified leads.
Installers and accountants can reach customers at moments when load shape or tariffs are salient.
Eligibility and suitability can be explained without acting as an undisclosed sales agent.

constraint_class.constraint: Consumer consent, marketing, withdrawal rights, energy-contract disclosures, and data protection
Access to meter status and interval consumption data
Trust in a calculator funded by sellers

concepts.prohibited_reliance: No dark patterns, hidden commissions, suppression of downside or lost price protection, unauthorized meter-data access, or claim that dynamic pricing is universally cheaper.
